capitals.name: Avanti (Ujjain)
capitals.note: The Pratihara page says Nagabhata I extended control from Mandor and took Avanti as his capital; the Ujjain origin (R.C. Majumdar, from the Harivamsha Purana of 783) is disputed by Dasharatha Sharma, who places the origin at Bhinmal/Jalor citing the Kuvalayamala of 778. The page names no capital for Vatsaraja. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Ujjain. The Nagabhata I page names Ujjain (not Mandor) as the capital he ruled from.

capitals.name: Kannauj
capitals.note: Nagabhata II 'proclaimed himself the King of Kannauj' in 816 and Kannauj became the Pratihara capital (Tripartite Struggle page); the Kannauj page gives no year and puts it after Dharmapala's death. capitals.name: Bari (across the Ganges east of Kannauj)
capitals.note: Mahmud of Ghazni page: after 1018 the Pratihara capital moved to Bari, which Rajyapala reached by fleeing 'across the Ganges to Bari forty miles east of Kannauj'. The page gives no year for the move and no coordinates; the position is forty miles (about 65 km) east of Kannauj, approximate. Razed by Mahmud in October 1020 (same page). Repair 2026-10-19: Bari lies outside Cliopatria's 980 and 1034 shapes (east edge 80.04 E), so the keyframes _1019 and 1034 add a 40 km circle round it.

Saurashtra and Sindh are removed because the Caliphate campaigns page keeps them outside any Gurjara realm: the Navsari grant of 739 lists Saindhava, Saurashtra and Gurjara as separate kingdoms, the Saindhavas repel Abbasid fleets in 756 and 776, and Sindh is the Arab province with its garrison cities. region.text: western and southern Rajasthan, Malwa and Gujarat, where the Arab raiders fought the Pratihara confederacy

ledger.note: 738: Nagabhata I leads a confederacy against the Arabs. The page: 'In this battle (738 CE), Nagabhata led a confederacy of Pratiharas to defeat the Muslim Arabs', naming Junaid and Tamin; the Caliphate campaigns page dates Junayd's governorship 723-726 and Tamim's from 726, so the names do not fit 738 (disagreement between pages), and says Ujjain was raided but 'Ujjain itself was not conquered'. The Nagabhata I page gives no year or site for the repulse and mentions neither Tamin nor 738.

region.text: Rajasthan and Gujarat

ledger.note: 743: the Arabs have lost their Rajasthan and Gujarat conquests. The page: the Arabs 'lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; al-Hakam died in battle in 740, which 'effectively ended the Arab presence to the east of Sindh'. The extent of Umayyad control is Blankinship's estimate, disputed on the page.

region.text: Gujarat, Malwa and Bundelkhand added in Cliopatria's 750 shape; the page is silent

ledger.note: 750: Cliopatria's Pratihara shape grows by about 0.25 M km2 (Gujarat, more of Malwa, part of Bundelkhand). No page dates this: the Pratihara page credits Nagabhata I with 'conquering Malwa as far as Gwalior and the port of Bharuch in Gujarat', undated, and the Nagabhata I page says he 'may have extended his control over Gurjaradesa' and may have taken Bharuch from the Chalukya feudatory Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin (Puri; no year); the nephews Devraj and Kakkuka are 'weak rulers'. The Dantidurga page has Dantidurga holding Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat by 750, hence the contest below. Bridging from the shape; the counterpart stays unrecorded because the pages name no loser for Malwa and Bundelkhand.

region.text: Malwa and southern Gujarat (Lata), where Dantidurga held 'Madhya Pradesh and Southern Gujarat' by 750

ledger.note: 750: Dantidurga's hold on Malwa and southern Gujarat meets the Pratihara shape. The page: 'By 750 AD Dantidurga had brought Madhya Pradesh and Southern Gujarat under his control' and he 'defeated the kings of Lata (Gujarat), Malwa, Tanka, Kalinga and Sheshas' (undated). It never names the Pratiharas, but the Tripartite Struggle page has him subdue a Pratihara king of Avanti, and the Nagabhata I page that Nagabhata 'appears to have been defeated by' him. Cliopatria keeps Malwa (86%) and half of Gujarat as Pratihara in 750-771, so the zone is drawn contested; the region is my reading.

region.text: Malwa and southern Gujarat (Lata)

ledger.note: 756: Dantidurga's reign ends (753-756 on his page, 735-756 in its succession table). No page records a Pratihara recovery or a treaty; the end year is bridging, and Cliopatria keeps Malwa Pratihara from 750 to 771.

region.text: Bundelkhand and Rajasthan added in Cliopatria's 772 shape; the page is silent

ledger.note: 772: Cliopatria's shape grows again (Gwalior side, Bundelkhand, Rajasthan), the year before Vatsaraja's reign on the page (775-805, 'master of western quarter'); no page dates the land. Bridging from the shape. Repair note: the Pratihara page has Vatsaraja (775-805) 'bringing much of Rajasthan under his control' (the Vatsaraja page: 780-800, 'from the Thar Desert in the west up to the frontiers of bengal in the east'), which fits the Rajasthan part; neither page dates it or names the states that lost the land.

region.text: Bundelkhand, Gwalior and the country east of Bundelkhand added in Cliopatria's 783 shape; the page is silent

ledger.note: 783: Cliopatria's shape reaches its maximum before 788. After the Doab, Awadh, Bihar and Magadha are removed (the page has no such annexation), what is left is Bundelkhand, Gwalior and a band at about 24 N between 80 E and 88 E (about 137,000 km2 in all); no page dates it. Bridging from the shape. Repair note: the Vatsaraja page dates none of his conquests (the Gwalior inscription of Bhoja says he 'subdued the entire world'), so Bundelkhand and Gwalior stay unrecorded.

region.text: Kannauj and the Doab under Indrayudha

ledger.note: 785: Vatsaraja takes the submission of Kannauj. The page: Vatsaraja invades Kannauj and defeats Indrayudha, who accepts his overlordship, without a year; Indrayudha succeeded in 783 (Ayudha page) and 785 is the page's start of the struggle ('a series of wars in northern India fought over the control of the throne of Kannauj'). Year is bridging. Repair note: the Vatsaraja page has an inscription of 795 recording his victories over Indrayudha and Bengal and dates the Kannauj campaign to no year, so the year stays bridging.

region.text: Malwa, Gwalior and the Doab, where Dhruva's army campaigned

ledger.note: c. 786: Dhruva of the Rashtrakutas crosses the Narmada into Malwa and tries to take Kannauj. The page: c. 786: Rashtrakuta ruler Dhruva crossed the Narmada into Malwa and tried to take Kannauj; the Tripartite page has him defeat Vatsaraja, who flees to the Maru deserts, and then Dharmapala in the Doab, and notes he only meant to raid, not conquer. The Pratihara page also, inconsistently, has Dhruva defeat Vatsaraja c. 800.

region.text: the country east of Bundelkhand (Baghelkhand to the Chota Nagpur side), about 24 N between 80 E and 88 E, that Cliopatria's 783 shape holds and its 788 shape drops

ledger.note: 788: the eastern part of Cliopatria's 783 growth leaves the shape, about 137,000 km2 (the 783 gain below carried it as 'Bundelkhand and Gwalior' only). No page has Pratihara rule there: the Vatsaraja page says his realm ran 'from the Thar Desert in the west up to the frontiers of bengal in the east', and the Tripartite Struggle page has Dhruva defeat Vatsaraja c. 786-790 and then Dharmapala in the Doab. Bridging from the shape; the corrected 788 keyframe uses the 793 land, so the band is out from 788 on.

region.text: Malwa, Gwalior and the Doab

ledger.note: 790: Dhruva goes home. The page: 'He thus returned to the South in 790.' The raid brought 'fame and vast booty but not more territory' (Rashtrakuta page); Cliopatria keeps the Pratiharas out of Malwa to 792.

region.text: Kannauj and the Doab, passed to Chakrayudha as a Pala vassal

ledger.note: c. 791: Dharmapala of the Palas takes Kannauj out of Pratihara overlordship. The page: Dharmapala invades Kannauj 'around 791', defeats Indrayudha and installs his brother Chakrayudha as a vassal; a footnote says the events 'may be assigned to about 791 A.D.'. Kannauj is not annexed.

region.text: Malwa, Lata (Gujarat) and Gwalior

ledger.note: 800: Govinda III's northern campaign. The Govinda III page: he 'conducted his northern campaign in 800 CE' and 'successfully obtained the submission of Gurjara-Pratihara emperor Nagabhata II'; after the conquest of Malwa he 'ensured the Paramara dynasty would rule as vassals of the Rashtrakutas in 800 CE'. The Paramara page has the Rashtrakutas expel the Gurjara-Pratiharas from Malwa between 808 and 812, and the Tripartite Struggle page has him defeat Nagabhata II near Gwalior and take Malwa, Lata and Mahakoshal (undated, reign 793-814). This event stood at his accession year, 793, in the first version; 800 is the page's year, the region is my reading.

region.text: Lata, southern Gujarat

ledger.note: c. 806: Lata passes to the Rashtrakutas. The page: Govinda III took Malwa, Lata, and Mahakoshal from the Gurjaras, undated between 793 and 814; Cliopatria's shape loses southern Gujarat in 806, and the Rashtrakuta page has him 'took firm hold over Gujarat'. Malwa is regained under Nagabhata II (Pratihara page), so only Lata is ledgered. Repair note: the Govinda III page records the conquest of Lata in an inscription of 813 and says he placed his brother Indra over it, so the loss lies between 800 and 813; 806 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: Malwa and Gwalior

ledger.note: 814: Govinda III dies and the Rashtrakuta threat ends. The page: 'the Rashtrakuta threat finally lapsed.'

region.text: the Doab and Kannauj, Chakrayudha's kingdom

ledger.note: 816: Nagabhata II takes Kannauj. 'In 816, Nagabhata II invaded the Doab, and defeated king Chakrayudha and proclaimed himself the King of Kannauj.' The Ayudha page: he 'invaded Kannauj, defeated Chakrayudha, and then made Kannauj his capital'; 'This marked the end of the Ayudhas'. The Pala battle of Monghyr follows, undated.

816: the Pratihara capital moves from Avanti (Ujjain) to Kannauj; the page makes Kannauj the Pratihara capital with the 816 victory. Kannauj page: Nagabhata II made it the capital after Dharmapala's death (no date).

region.text: Bundelkhand outside the Doab, Gwalior and Malwa: the Chandelas of Bundelkhand / Jejakabhukti

ledger.note: 836 and the years after: the Chandelas of Bundelkhand acknowledge Mihira Bhoja. The Bhoja page lists them among kingdoms that acknowledged his suzerainty without a year; Bhoja's reign begins 836, hence the year (bridging). The Chandela page says they were 'originally vassals of the Gurjara-Pratiharas' (Nannuka, the founder, c. 831-845) and the Pratihara page that the Khajuraho temples were built by 'their vassals, the Chandelas of Bundelkhand'. The keyframes from 836 draw this land as vassal tint, not as direct land (repair 2026-10-19: the first version drew 49-78% of Bundelkhand as direct land as well).

region.text: Kutch and the fort of Sindan

ledger.note: 842: Mihira Bhoja drives the Arabs out of Kutch. The page: he pushed them out of Kutch and evicted them from the fort of Sindan 'between 833 and 842' (it also dates the Arab conflicts to the early 8th century, a contradiction); the year is the end of the range. Cliopatria's shapes do not include Kutch. The Pratihara page's account (a summary, not a quotation) has him push the Arabs out of Kutch and parts of Sindh between 833 and 842; the Sindh part is ledgered with the 860 shape because no page names it.

region.text: Gujaratra and Lata Parvarta: Gujarat without Saurashtra and Kutch

ledger.note: 860: Bhoja's Gujarat, as Cliopatria draws it. The Bhoja page lists Gujaratra and Lata Parvarta among his conquests, says he backed a claimant against Dhruva II of Gujarat (repulsed, undated), kept parts of Gujarat and Malwa, and by 885 had 'successfully exterminated the Gujarat Rashtrakuta line' (its sources conflict); no page gives the year of the conquest, 860 is Cliopatria's. Repair 2026-10-19: Saurashtra is no longer part of this gain (the first version named the Rashtrakutas as its loser, against the dossier's own keyframes 750-850): the Bhoja page does not name Saurashtra, the Saindhava page has the Saindhavas ruling western Saurashtra c. 735 to c. 920, and the Pratihara link the pages do give is the Chavda feudatory of 914 (below).

region.text: the Sindh strip (16% of Sindh) that Cliopatria's 860 shape holds

ledger.note: 860: Cliopatria's Pratihara shape holds 16% of Sindh from 860, overlapping its Habbari shape. The Pratihara page says Bhoja pushed the Arabs out of Kutch and parts of Sindh between 833 and 842 (WebFetch summary, not a quotation), which is the only page support for a Pratihara hold in Sindh; the year is Cliopatria's. The Habbari page (Habbaris at Mansura from 854, central and southern Sindh) never mentions the Pratiharas. The loss is ledgered at 936.

region.text: Saurashtra, where the Chapa Dharanivaraha of Vardhamana (modern Wadhwan) was Mahipala's feudatory

ledger.note: 914: Saurashtra under Pratihara suzerainty. The Chavda page: 'Dharanivaraha's Haddala grant dated Shaka 836 (914 CE) mentions himself as Chapas of Vardhamana', 'as a feudatory of Gurjara-Pratiharya [Mahipaladeva]' (the Mahipala I page: a Chapa ruler at Vardhamana, modern Wadhwan, 'a feudatory of Mahipala ... in his grant dated 914'). The grant names one chief; the whole of Saurashtra as vassal tint is my reading, because Cliopatria draws Saurashtra as direct land from 860 to 935 and the Saindhava page has the Saindhavas ruling western Saurashtra c. 735 to c. 920 without calling them Pratihara feudatories. Before 914 no page ties Saurashtra to the Pratiharas, so it is not drawn.

region.text: Kannauj and the Ganges-Yamuna doab

ledger.note: c. 916: Indra III of the Rashtrakutas sacks Kannauj. The page: c. 916: Indra III sacked Kannauj. The Pratiharas later regained the city. The Indra III page says Kannauj was 'completely destroyed', Mahipala I fled 'as if struck by lightning', and the Rashtrakutas 'were actually able to hold Kannauj until c. 916'; the coronation was 24 February 915. The Mahipala I page adds that the campaign 'did not influence Kannauj much'.

region.text: Kannauj and the doab

ledger.note: 926: Kannauj is back in Pratihara hands. The page says only that the Pratiharas later regained the city; Cliopatria restores Kannauj in 926. The Chandela page has the Chandela Harsha 'restoring the rule of the Pratihara king Mahipala'. Year is bridging. Repair note: the Mahipala I page says Indra III's campaign 'did not influence Kannauj much' and that Mahipala soon revived the city, and the Chandela page has Harsha (c. 905-925) helping to restore Mahipala; no page gives a year, so 926 is an upper bound and the real contest may have been much shorter.

region.text: Ujjain and the Malwa plateau

ledger.note: 936: Malwa passes to the Paramaras. The page: the Paramaras of Malwa, Kalachuris, Tomaras and Chahamanas declared independence during Mahipala I's weakness (912-944), without years; Cliopatria's shape loses most of Malwa in 936; Cliopatria's Paramara row starts 980. Bridging. Repair note: the Paramara page does not support a Paramara break-away from the Pratiharas in 936: it has the Paramaras 'most probably subordinates of the Rashtrakutas in the 9th century', Siyaka a feudatory of Krishna III in the Harsola plates of 949, and the first independent sovereignty only c. 972; a Pratapgarh inscription of 945-946 is said to record that a Pratihara king Mahendrapala 'recaptured Malwa'. The year and the taker (Rashtrakutas or Paramaras) are therefore unsettled; the event stays Cliopatria's, confidence 1.

region.text: the Sindh strip (16% of Sindh) shared with the Habbaris in Cliopatria

ledger.note: 936: the Sindh part of the shape is dropped. The pages opened do not discuss Sindh after the Arabs; Cliopatria's Pratihara and Habbari shapes overlap there from 860 and the overlap ends in 936. A gap-filler should open the Habbari page. Repair note: the Habbari page puts the Habbaris in central and southern Sindh from Mansura (capital 883; a Hindu Raja of Aror was their subordinate) and does not mention the Pratiharas, so the page is silent on who held the strip in 860-935.

region.text: Gujarat (Anahilavada) and Kutch

ledger.note: 942: Gujarat and Kutch leave the Pratihara map when Mularaja founds the Chaulukya state. The Chavda page: Mularaja 'overthrew him in 942' (the last Chavda king; 'c. 942' in the body); the Chaulukya page says he 'supplanted the last ruler of the Chavda dynasty around 940 CE' at Anahilavada and has him defeat Graharipu of Saurashtra (per Hemachandra, reported). Neither page says the land was Pratihara; the Chavda page gives no year for any Pratihara hold on Gujarat. Cliopatria's shape drops most of Gujarat, Kutch and Saurashtra in 936 and the rest in 947; the first version dated this loss 940 and made it fall into the gap between the 936 shape and the ledger, now 942 with the 936 keyframe holding both to 941. Saurashtra is not part of this loss: it leaves the vassal tint (below).

region.text: Saurashtra

ledger.note: c. 942: Saurashtra leaves the Pratihara tint when Mularaja overthrows the last Chavda king ('in 942', Chavda page) and defeats Graharipu of Saurashtra (Chaulukya page). The Chavdas of Vardhamana are not said to fall in 942, and the Saindhava page ends the Saindhavas between 920 and 987 and has a 987 inscription of a probable Chaulukya vassal; bridging.

region.text: the Gujarat-Rajasthan border fringe (about 22-26 N, 72-74 E) that Cliopatria's 947 shape drops

ledger.note: 947: about 25,000 km2 of southern Rajasthan and the Gujarat border leave Cliopatria's shape, all of it inside Cliopatria's Chaulukya shape that begins in 947. The Chaulukya page puts Mularaja at Anahilavada around 940 and says nothing about this fringe or about Pratihara land; bridging from the shape.

region.text: Bundelkhand outside the Doab, Gwalior and Malwa: the Chandela domain

ledger.note: c. 950: the Chandelas stop acknowledging the Pratiharas. The Chandela page: Yashovarman (c. 925-950) 'continued to acknowledge the Pratihara suzerainty, but became practically independent'; Dhanga (c. 950-999) mentions no Pratihara overlord, 'This indicates that Dhanga formally established the Chandela sovereignty.' The Pratihara page instead lists the Chandelas of Bundelkhand among the feudatories that declared independence during the weakness of the Pratiharas under Mahipala I (912-944), without years; the two pages disagree by up to forty years, and the ledger follows the Chandela page, whose rulers' records it can read.

region.text: Gwalior

ledger.note: c. 950: the Chandelas take Gwalior. The Pratihara page: 'the Chandelas captured the strategic fortress of Gwalior in central India around 950.' (The Chandela page does not credit Yashovarman with Gwalior; it has the Kachchhapaghatas of Gwalior as later Chandela subordinates.) Bundelkhand is not part of this loss in the repaired version: it was a Chandela vassal land since 836 and its end is the vassal_end above.

region.text: Rajasthan

ledger.note: 960: Rajasthan is in the hands of its former feudatories. The page: the Rajasthan feudatories took control of Rajasthan by the 10th century and the Chahamanas of Shakambhari declared independence, without years; Cliopatria's shape drops to the Kannauj rump in 960 and its Chauhan row starts 980. Repair note: the Chahamana page has Vakpatiraja I (917-944) 'attempt to overthrow the Gurjara-Pratihara suzerainty', Simharaja (944-971) assume the title Maharajadhiraja, and lists the dynasty as 'Vassals of the Pratiharas (at least 784–948)', which brackets independence between about 948 and 971 and does not contradict 960.

region.text: the rest of the Malwa plateau

ledger.note: 960: what is left of Malwa goes to the Paramaras (see 936). Year is Cliopatria's. The Paramara page gives no year for a Paramara break-away from the Pratiharas (see 936).

region.text: Kannauj and the seven forts around it

ledger.note: 1018: Mahmud of Ghazni marches on Kannauj. 'He arrived on 20 December 1018.' Rajyapala 'fled across the Ganges to Bari forty miles east of Kannauj'; Mahmud took seven forts, plundered the city. After Sirwasa (2 December), Baran, Mahaban and Mathura he reached Kannauj; Kannauj was left under local rulers (the page says conquered kingdoms were generally left under local vassals).

1019: the Pratihara seat moves to Bari. Mahmud page: the Pratihara capital moved to Bari; no year is given, so 1019 (after the 1018 flight) is bridging. The Pratihara page does not mention Bari at all; the /wiki/Rajyapala article is the Pala king (925-962), and no Pratihara Rajyapala article was found, so the year stays bridging.

region.text: the Doab outside the Kannauj rump and the Bari circle

ledger.note: 1019: the Pratihara state shrinks from the Doab to Cliopatria's rump round Kannauj plus Bari. The Pratihara page has the dynasty controlling 'little more than the Gangetic Doab' at the end of the tenth century, and the Mahmud page has Rajyapala flee 'across the Ganges to Bari forty miles east of Kannauj' after the sacks of Baran, Mahaban, Mathura and Kannauj (December 1018). No page says who held the rest of the Doab afterwards (the Mahmud page says conquered kingdoms were generally left under local rulers; the Gahadavalas hold Kannauj from about 1090, Kannauj page). Bridging, from the rump.

region.text: Kannauj and the Doab

ledger.note: January 1019: Mahmud turns back to Ghazni after the battle at Sharwa on 6 January. The Pratihara page: Rajyapala was later killed by the Chandela ruler Vidyadhara; the Chandela page says for 'fleeing his capital instead of fighting'. The Mahmud page also has Trilochanpala beaten at the Ramganga in October 1020 and Bari razed.

region.text: Kannauj and the Bari rump

ledger.note: 1036: Jasapala, the last Pratihara ruler of Kannauj, dies. The page: 1036: Jasapala, the last Pratihara ruler of Kannauj, died. Several small branches survive the Ghaznavid invasions, one ruling Mandore until the 14th century; the Gahadavalas hold Kannauj from about 1090.

wars.name: Arab campaigns in Rajasthan and Gujarat
wars.outcome: Junayd (723-726) 'recaptured Sindh, conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan' but not Ujjain; the Arabs 'lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; the Chalukya general Pulakeshin defeated them at Navsari in 739; al-Hakam died fighting in 740.
wars.note: The Pratihara page puts Nagabhata I's victory over Junaid and Tamin in 738; the Caliphate page dates the Gwalior inscription's 'Valacha Mlecchas' c. 725 and doubts the Arab identification. Nagabhata's part is therefore uncertain. The campaigns began in 723 under Junayd (Caliphate campaigns page); the war is clipped to the state's 730 start (reviewer sa-03-c).

wars.name: Dantidurga's subjugation of the Avanti Pratiharas
wars.outcome: The Dantidurga page says 'By 750 AD Dantidurga had brought Madhya Pradesh and Southern Gujarat under his control' and that he defeated the kings of Lata, Malwa and others (undated); the Tripartite Struggle page has him subdue a Pratihara king of Avanti, who acted as his door-keeper; the Rashtrakuta page says he 'defeated the Gurjaras'. No land is said to have changed hands.
wars.note: Repaired 2026-10-19: the first version dated the war 735-756 from the Tripartite page's reign for Dantidurga; the Dantidurga page has the reign as 753-756 in its text and infobox and 735-756 in its succession table, and its one dated claim is 750. The Cliopatria Pratihara shape keeps Malwa throughout, so the zone is drawn as contested 750-756.

wars.name: Tripartite Struggle

zones.text: the Ganges-Yamuna doab and Kannauj, 'control of the throne of Kannauj'

wars.outcome: Pratihara victory in 816: Nagabhata II defeats Chakrayudha and proclaims himself king of Kannauj; before that Vatsaraja (overlord), Dhruva (raid, home in 790), Dharmapala (Chakrayudha as Pala vassal c. 791) and Govinda III (submission of Dharmapala and Chakrayudha) each held or raided Kannauj.
wars.note: The page gives the struggle as 785-816; the Monghyr battle against Dharmapala after 816 is undated.

wars.name: Bhoja's wars against the Arabs of Sind

zones.text: Kutch and the fort of Sindan

wars.outcome: Bhoja evicted the Arabs from Sindan and pushed them out of Kutch.
wars.note: The page also dates Arab conflicts to the 'early 8th century' and names Imran ibn-Musa without a year.

wars.name: Battle of Ujjain (Krishna II and Bhoja)
wars.outcome: Krishna II defeated the Pratiharas at Ujjain: 'Around 880' in one passage, 'Sometime before 888' in another. The page does not say land changed hands, and Cliopatria's Pratihara shape keeps Malwa to 921.

wars.name: Indra III's invasion of the doab
wars.outcome: Indra III sacked Kannauj c. 916 and Mahipala I fled; the Rashtrakutas held the city only briefly and the Pratiharas regained it (year not on the page).
wars.note: Indra III's coronation was 24 February 915 (Indra III page).

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Kannauj

zones.text: Kannauj and the forts of the doab

wars.outcome: Mahmud reaches Kannauj on 20 December 1018, Rajyapala flees to Bari, the city is plundered and left under local rulers; Mahmud is at Sharwa on 6 January 1019.

wars.name: Ghaznavid campaigns against Trilochanpala and Vidyadhara
wars.outcome: October 1020: Trilochanpala beaten at the Ramganga, Bari razed; 1022 Gwalior surrenders and Vidyadhara pays tribute and keeps fifteen fortresses.
wars.note: The page's 1019 date for the Kalinjar operations is absent; it gives 1020 and 1022.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Narmada is the one river frontier the pages name ('the Narmada River in the south' in Bhoja's reign). Frontiers with the feudatories (Chandelas, Guhilas, Chahamanas, Paramaras) and the Rashtrakuta marches in Malwa and Gujarat swing and are approximate.
A Kannauj rump under Ghaznavid pressure; no frontier is described.

sources.note: Reign c. 730-760, capital Ujjain, Bharuch and Gurjaradesa only as "may have", defeat by Dantidurga.

sources.title: Dantidurga
sources.note: "By 750 AD" Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat; reign 753-756 (text) or 735-756 (table).

sources.title: Vatsaraja
sources.note: Reign 780-800 on his page, Rajasthan to Bengal, the 795 inscription, no date for Kannauj.

sources.title: Govinda III
sources.note: Northern campaign in 800, Malwa and Lata, Lata inscription of 813.

sources.title: Mahipala I
sources.note: Reign 913-944, Indra III and Kannauj "did not influence Kannauj much", Dharanivaraha of Vardhamana, 914. (The reviewer's URL Mahipala_I_(Pratihara_dynasty) did not load; the article is at this title.)

sources.title: Mahendrapala I
sources.note: Reign c. 885-c. 910, Bhoja II 910-913, extent.

sources.title: Saindhava dynasty
sources.note: Western Saurashtra c. 735-c. 920, Agguka I and the Arabs in 776, end between 920 and 987.

sources.title: Chavda dynasty
sources.note: Dharanivaraha of Vardhamana as feudatory of Mahipala in 914; Mularaja overthrows the last Chavda in 942.

sources.title: Habbari dynasty
sources.note: Mansura, central and southern Sindh, 854-1024; no mention of the Pratiharas.

sources.title: Paramara dynasty
sources.note: Rashtrakuta subordinates in the 9th century, expulsion of the Pratiharas from Malwa 808-812, Harsola plates 949, independence c. 972.

sources.title: Chahamanas of Shakambhari
sources.note: Vassals of the Pratiharas (at least 784-948), Vakpatiraja I 917-944, Simharaja Maharajadhiraja 944-971.

notes:
Page budget: 10 pages opened (9 for the state plus the Kannauj article shared with kannauj-varman-dynasty). The Pratihara infobox gives no area, no capital and no ruler names, so no area comparison could be made and the keyframes are judged by what the pages say about land. Cliopatria's shapes 750-805 are corrected only where a page contradicts them (Kannauj before 816, Bihar and Magadha in 783, Saurashtra and Sindh), and the unexplained growth in 750, 772 and 783 is ledgered at confidence 1 with the counterpart unrecorded (page silent): a gap-filler should open the pages of Dantidurga, Vatsaraja and Nagabhata I. Not read: Habbari dynasty (Sindh overlap 860-935), Nagabhata I, Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mahendrapala I, Mahipala I and Rajyapala articles, Chauhan, Paramara and Gahadavala pages, Seshat. Rulers: a partial strip (Nagabhata I, then Vatsaraja to Mahipala I, 730-944) was added in the repair; the pages open give no reign years for Devraj, Kakkuka (760-775) or for the rulers of 944-1036. The Ayudha dynasty is written into kannauj-varman-dynasty as the same Kannauj state (rename in 770), ending in the 816 gain here. Counterparts with no dossier: Chavdas of Bhillamala, Kalachuris of Tripuri/Mahakoshal, Tomaras of Haryana, Guhilas of Chatsu, Saindhavas of Saurashtra, Arabs of Sind. Gazetteer: Mandor (Nagabhata I's base, near Jodhpur) is not a place name in the gazetteer; Marwar stands in for it. 'Bari' east of Kannauj is not a region; Kannauj with a radius stands in. The Kannauj rump from 960 is the only shape with a correction of years and not land.
